output.summary: A branching annual native to temperate North Africa, Europe and parts of western Asia, it has bristly stems and a slender taproot that does not swell like cultivated radish. Its flowers are usually white but may be yellow or purple. All tender parts are edible; the pods and washed outer root skin can also be eaten.
output.edibilityNote: Tender parts, including spicy leaves and flowers, are edible; seedpods and the washed outer skin of the root can also be eaten.
